Serum protein electrophoresis: Multiple myeloma may be associated with osteoporosis

Albumin-corrected (or ionised) calcium; phosphate; parathyroid hormone (PTH); alkaline phosphatase, vitamin D, renal function and, in an older man with back pain, serum protein electrophoresis and a skeletal survey to look for myeloma or bone metastases.

qs.q: A patient with suspected osteoporosis undergoes baseline laboratory studies to rule out secondary causes. Which condition should be evaluated using serum protein electrophoresis?
qs.e: Serum protein electrophoresis is used to check for multiple myeloma, which may be associated with osteoporosis. Thyroid dysfunction, vitamin D levels, and male hypogonadism are assessed using TSH, 25-hydroxyvitamin D, and testosterone/gonadotropins respectively.

qs.q: A 55-year-old man presents with visual disturbances, fatigue and epistaxis. Serum protein electrophoresis shows a monoclonal IgM spike. Bone marrow biopsy reveals lymphoplasmacytoid infiltration. What gene mutation is present in >90% of cases?
qs.e: This is Waldenström's macroglobulinaemia (LPL). MYD88 mutation is present in >90% and is near-diagnostic.
